text:
sara: quick follow-up from the rfc review — proposing a compatibility facade for v3->v4 migration that lives at ingress and does payload translation + telemetry tagging. goal: minimal SDK churn for customers.

mike: ingress transformation makes sense for central control, but curious about perf implications. are we talking per-request JSON rewrite?

sara: yes, rule-based rewrites initially. think of it as fast mappings + small transformation functions. target added latency <=5ms p50.

dan: for enterprise/private customers the facade would be in their control plane — we need a deployment artifact that can run in-vpc/on-prem. SDK-only approach pushes to customers and will be messy.

sophia: latency budget is tight. where do we add caching? prefix caching still applies but transformations could change cache keys. need a deterministic canonicalization step.

raj: idea: precompile common mappings into a tiny VM (like lua or wasm) so translations are JIT-free. avoids overhead of heavy JSON parsing on the hot path. we can keep a fallback path for complex cases.

leo: telemetry: add headers/fields: "migration_cohort", "transform_version", "transformation_applied". these must appear in request logs and billing traces. also tag responses for QA validation.

mike: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag per-tenant, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with staged validation. include an opt-in header for customers who want to test early.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: compat-facade v1 -> canary cluster at 2025-11-12T02:00Z (automated).

sophia: tests: add a prompt-sample matrix to run through both v3 and v4 transforms and diff outputs. signal mismatches where the transformed request produces meaningfully different model outputs. we need a regression threshold.

raj: runbook: automatic rollback if error-rate increase >0.5% or p95 latency increases by 20% relative to baseline. also add a manual emergency toggle in console.

dan: for on-prem customers that are air-gapped we should provide a migration helper binary (offline translator) and a small preflight tool that checks payload compatibility against local model versions. docs + example scripts.

leo: security note: @security-review required for any transformation that touches user-provided tool-calls or function-calling fields. don't rewrite call targets silently.

sara: agreed — transformation rules must be opt-in for anything that mutates instructions/function calls. by default only structural compatibility edits (field rename, envelope shape) are allowed.

mike: sample transform snippet for review:

```
# facade rule: rename "user_prompt" -> "input.text" and lift "metadata.ctx" -> "input.ctx"
{
  "match": {"path": "user_prompt"},
  "rewrite": {"to": "input.text"}
}
```

raj: add a checksum header so we can detect when a transform was applied and validate determinism across environments. e.g., `X-Compat-Transform: v1-<hash>`

sophia: also add a lightweight metric: `compat.transform.latency_ms` to monitor perf regressions over time.

dan: docs runbook checklist: migration guide, tenant opt-in steps, SDK helper for offline customers, FAQ for edge cases, and a small troubleshooting section with commands to dump canonicalized payloads.

sara: next steps: finalize transform API spec, prototype runtime (wasm suggestion), and add telemetry keys. i'll spin up a short spike this week and share results in here. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — will pair on durability tests. :eyes:

leo: tagging @security for the review invite.

infra-bot: note: created jira RED-INF-4231 "compatibility facade spike": https://jira.redwood.example/browse/RED-INF-4231

sara: placing this in the backlog for the architecture weekly sync. if anyone objects to the ingress-first posture speak now or DM.
